FROM: Controller's Office

Ridgeview manufactures industrial fasteners across three product lines. Titan uses dollar-value LIFO for its steel products division. The relevant LIFO layers are: 2018 layer: 11,500 units at $42.00/unit; 2019 layer: 9,800 units at $45.80/unit; 2020 layer: 12,300 units at $51.30/unit; 2021 layer: 8,200 units at $58.75/unit; 2022 layer: 6,200 units at $67.20/unit. Mr. Ross asks: 'What is the Q3 P&L impact of this LIFO liquidation, and what disclosure is required?'

Choices.A: The liquidation releases older, lower-cost LIFO layers into COGS (replacing $71.50 current cost with costs as low as $42.00), increasing Q3 gross profit. Disclosure is required under ASC 270-10-50-6 because the non-recurring gain materially distorts comparability of interim operating results. However, the gain is embedded in COGS — it is NOT presented as a separate income statement line item but disclosed in the notes to the interim financial statements.
Choices.B: The liquidation has no P&L impact because LIFO is a cost flow assumption, not a physical flow. Titan will replenish inventory in Q4, restoring the LIFO layers, so the Q3 liquidation is a temporary phenomenon that self-corrects. No separate disclosure is required; Titan should note the strike in MD&A without quantifying the LIFO effect.

ASC 270 requires separate presentation of material and unusual items. The gain is recognized in Q3 and reverses when inventory is replenished in Q4, with the Q4 reversal also separately presented.
Choices.D: Titan should neutralize the income effect by recording a LIFO liquidation reserve equal to the difference between replacement cost and the liquidated layer costs (debit COGS, credit LIFO liquidation reserve). Under the matching principle, COGS should reflect current replacement cost regardless of LIFO layers; the reserve defers the liquidation gain until inventory is physically replaced.

Cascade is finalizing a 10-year lease for a regional distribution center. Key terms: (1) Annual lease payments of $280,000, payable at year-end. Cascade's incremental borrowing rate is 6.5%. (2) The building's estimated economic life is 25 years; its fair value at lease commencement is $3,400,000. (3) The lease contains a bargain purchase option allowing Cascade to buy the building for $850,000 at the end of year 10; the expected fair value at that date is estimated at $1,800,000. (4) The lease also contains two 5-year renewal options at market rates; Cascade is undecided about exercising them. (5) Cascade cannot direct the use of the building without the lessor's consent for major structural modifications. (6) The present value of the 10 annual lease payments, discounted at 6.5%, is approximately $2,009,000. (7) The present value of the bargain purchase option payment ($850,000 discounted 10 years at 6.5%) is approximately $453,000. The controller's deputy argues the lease is operating because the lease term (10 years) is only 40% of the economic life (25 years), below the 75% bright-line test. Mr. Chen asks: 'Under ASC 842, is this an operating lease or a finance lease, and what is the initial right-of-use asset and lease liability?'

Choices.A: Operating lease. The lease term (10 years) is 40% of the economic life (25 years), well below the major-part threshold. The bargain purchase option does not factor into lease classification because it is exercisable only at the end of the term and Cascade is undecided. Present value of lease payments ($2,009,000) is approximately 59% of fair value, below the substantially-all threshold. Initial ROU asset and lease liability: $2,009,000.
Choices.B: Finance lease. The bargain purchase option makes it reasonably certain that Cascade will acquire the building at year 10, satisfying ASC 842-10-25-2(d). The lease term is therefore the full economic life of the asset, making the lease-term test moot. Cascade must classify as a finance lease. Initial ROU asset and lease liability: present value of lease payments ($2,009,000) plus present value of the bargain purchase option exercise price ($453,000) = $2,462,000.
Choices.C: Operating lease. Although the bargain purchase option is relevant, it affects only the lease payments measurement — not classification. Under ASC 842-10-25-2, the five classification tests are applied independently, and Cascade fails each: the lease term is not a major part of economic life, the present value test is not met, and there is no transfer of ownership. Initial ROU asset and lease liability: $2,462,000 (including the purchase option payment because the option is a bargain).
Choices.D: Finance lease. The present value of lease payments plus the bargain purchase option exercise price ($2,462,000) equals 72.4% of the building's fair value. Substantially all (typically 90%+) of the fair value of the underlying asset — the present value criterion is NOT met. However, the bargain purchase option independently triggers finance lease classification under ASC 842-10-25-2(d). The initial ROU asset and lease liability equal $2,462,000.

sectionA.Stem: Axion Technologies develops software for autonomous vehicle systems. Under U.S. GAAP, all R&D costs are expensed as incurred, resulting in reported losses of $8.4 million this year. Axion is considering a European stock exchange listing that would require IFRS reporting. Under IAS 38, $3.2 million of development costs would qualify for capitalization as they meet the criteria for technical feasibility, intent to complete, and ability to use or sell. The CFO asks the controller for a recommendation on which accounting framework best reflects Axion's economic performance to investors. What recommendation should the controller present?

Choices.A: Recommend U.S. GAAP and continued expensing. The conservative treatment protects investors from overstated asset values and is consistent with the principle that R&D outcomes are inherently uncertain. Reported losses accurately reflect the cash invested in development activities, which is the most decision-useful information for investors.
Choices.B: Recommend IFRS reporting because IAS 38 allows capitalization of qualifying development costs, which better reflects the economic value created by Axion's investments. Under IFRS, the $3.2 million would be recognized as an intangible asset and amortized over the software's useful life, providing a more faithful representation of the company's financial position and the future benefits expected from its development pipeline.
Choices.C: Recommend a blended approach: maintain U.S. GAAP as the primary reporting framework but present non-GAAP supplemental disclosures that capitalize and amortize qualifying development costs. This gives investors both the conservative GAAP framework and additional information about the value of Axion's development investments.
Choices.D: Recommend that neither framework is clearly superior. The choice between expensing and capitalizing development costs is ultimately a matter of accounting policy preference with no objective economic basis. Choices.B: Zero variable costs for one of the products
Choices.C: A constant sales mix between the two products
Choices.D: Equal selling prices for both products

sectionDD.ExplanationCorrect: Multi-product CVP analysis requires assuming a constant sales mix in order to compute a single, meaningful weighted-average break-even point.
